paper.title_en: Electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks in a coupled-channel unitary approach
paper.abstract_en: We study the electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks $P_c(4312)$, $P_c(4440)$ and $P_c(4457)$ and of their four heavy-quark spin partners, treated as $\bar D^{(*)}Σ_c^{(*)}$ hadronic molecules. The states are poles of a coupled-channel unitary amplitude with a vector-meson exchange kernel that respects heavy-quark spin symmetry. The form factors are the residues at the double pole of the photon-coupled amplitude. The current consists of one-body currents and a photon--four-hadron vertex, which we construct for this channel space. Its gauged-kernel part ensures the charge normalization through the compositeness sum rule, while its contact parts contain couplings that the model does not determine. For $J^P=\tfrac12^-$, $\tfrac12^-$, $\tfrac32^-$ and pointlike constituents, the mean squared distances between the constituents of the three observed states are $0.85-0.47i$, $0.35-0.18i$ and $1.76-0.57i\,\mathrm{fm}^2$. Within $2\%$, they equal the zero-range value $1/(4μ_{\rm red} B_c)$, with reduced mass $μ_{\rm red}$ and complex binding energy $B_c$, times the effective-range factor of the amplitude. The real parts of the magnetic moments are $1.7$, $-0.9$ and $1.3\,μ_N$, within $11\%$ of the additive moments of the constituents. Variations of the constituent moments and of the magnetic contact couplings within bounds from dimensional analysis give the ranges $0.8$ to $2.0$, $-1.3$ to $-0.2$ and $0.2$ to $1.8\,μ_N$. The charge radii depend also on the constituent structure and on electric contact currents. The photon loops of open channels have a triangle singularity at spacelike momentum transfer. We specify the analytic continuation of the residue in $Q^2$ and give the difference between its two adjacent branches in closed form.
